es: Valorar si una retroalimentación es específica, respetuosa y accionable, y decidir qué habría que mejorar en las que no lo son.

vocabulary.es: accionable; que se puede poner en práctica

teaching.en: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes, which is a specific observation that anyone on the pitch could confirm.
teaching.es: Me fijé en que hiciste con prisa tus dos últimos pases, y esa es una observación concreta que cualquiera en el campo podría confirmar.
teaching.explanationEs: Específica: describe un hecho que se vio, no una opinión.
segments: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes, which is
a specific observation that anyone on the pitch could confirm.
teaching.audioText: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes, which is a specific observation that anyone on the pitch could confirm.

teaching.en: That was terrible, and you never listen to anybody: that kind of comment is disrespectful, and it does not tell you what to do next.
teaching.es: Eso fue terrible y nunca escuchas a nadie: ese tipo de comentario es irrespetuoso y no te dice qué hacer después.
teaching.explanationEs: Irrespetuosa: ataca a la persona con terrible y never, y no dice qué hacer.
segments: That was terrible, and you never listen to anybody: that kind of comment
is disrespectful, and it does not tell you what to do next.
teaching.audioText: That was terrible, and you never listen to anybody: that kind of comment is disrespectful, and it does not tell you what to do next.

teaching.en: Next time, breathe before you shoot and stay calm, because a steady start gives you more time to choose your shot.
teaching.es: La próxima vez, respira antes de disparar y mantén la calma, porque un comienzo sereno te da más tiempo para elegir tu tiro.
teaching.explanationEs: Accionable: Next time + imperativo = un paso que se puede dar.
segments: Next time, breathe before you shoot and stay calm, because a
steady start gives you more time to choose your shot.
teaching.audioText: Next time, breathe before you shoot and stay calm, because a steady start gives you more time to choose your shot.

teaching.en: I suggest you practise your left foot twice a week; that is an actionable step, because you can start it tomorrow.
teaching.es: Te sugiero que practiques tu pie izquierdo dos veces por semana; es un paso accionable, porque puedes empezarlo mañana.
teaching.explanationEs: I suggest you + verbo base: sugerencia concreta, sin to.
segments: I suggest you practise your left foot twice a week; that
is an actionable step, because you can start it tomorrow.
teaching.audioText: I suggest you practise your left foot twice a week; that is an actionable step, because you can start it tomorrow.

teaching.en: Your talk was helpful because you gave clear examples, and your respectful tone made it easy for the group to listen.
teaching.es: Tu charla fue útil porque diste ejemplos claros, y tu tono respetuoso hizo que al grupo le resultara fácil escuchar.
teaching.explanationEs: Valorar con un motivo: because + dato concreto.
segments: Your talk was helpful because you gave clear examples, and your
respectful tone made it easy for the group to listen.
teaching.audioText: Your talk was helpful because you gave clear examples, and your respectful tone made it easy for the group to listen.

teaching.en: That was good, I guess, is only a vague comment, so ask politely: could you be more specific about what worked?
teaching.es: «Estuvo bien, supongo» es solo un comentario vago, así que pregunta con educación: ¿podrías ser más concreto sobre qué funcionó?
teaching.explanationEs: Ante un comentario vago, pide concreción con Could you be more specific?
segments: That was good, I guess, is only a vague comment, so
ask politely: could you be more specific about what worked?
teaching.audioText: That was good, I guess, is only a vague comment, so ask politely: could you be more specific about what worked?

prompt.es: ¿Qué comentario es específico y respetuoso a la vez?

choices.text: You always rush everything you do on the pitch.
That was not very good, but I am sure you will improve.
I noticed that you rushed your last two passes.

feedback.es: Solo el comentario sobre los dos últimos pases cita un hecho concreto sin juzgar a la persona.

hint.es: Busca el que cita un hecho que se vio, sin always ni never.

prompt.es: Completa: «“Estuvo bien, supongo” es un comentario vago: no dice qué repetir.»

feedback.es: Un comentario vago suena amable, pero no cita ningún hecho ni dice qué hacer.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo contrario a specific.

origin.text: That was good, I guess is a ___ comment: it does not tell you what to repeat or what to change.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La próxima vez, respira antes de disparar y mantén la calma.»

answer.text: Next time breathe before you shoot and stay calm

feedback.es: Next time + imperativo es la estructura de un paso accionable.

hint.es: Empieza por Next time y acaba con stay calm.

prompt.es: Escucha los comentarios del entrenador y elige cuál es específico y accionable.

choices.text: The one about the rushed passes and breathing before the next pass.
The one that says the talk was good, I guess.
The one that says that the player never listens to anybody at all.

feedback.es: Solo el segundo comentario cita un hecho (pases apresurados) y un paso que se puede dar (respirar antes de pasar).

origin.audio: After the tournament, three players received comments from their coach. To the first he said: That was terrible, you never listen. To the second he said: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes, so next time, breathe before you pass and stay calm. To the third he said: That was good, I guess. The third player looked confused and asked: Could you be more specific? The coach thought for a moment and answered: Your talk to the group was helpful because you gave clear examples.

prompt.es: Con los mismos comentarios, elige qué hace el tercer jugador para mejorar lo que recibe.

choices.text: He tells the coach that the comment was disrespectful.
He asks the coach to be more specific.
He accepts the comment and thanks the coach.

feedback.es: El tercer jugador pide concreción con «Could you be more specific?» y consigue un motivo claro.

origin.audio: After the tournament, three players received comments from their coach. To the first he said: That was terrible, you never listen. To the second he said: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes, so next time, breathe before you pass and stay calm. To the third he said: That was good, I guess. The third player looked confused and asked: Could you be more specific? The coach thought for a moment and answered: Your talk to the group was helpful because you gave clear examples.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada comentario con el criterio que incumple o cumple.

pairs: I noticed that you lost the ball three times.

feedback.es: El primero ataca a la persona, el segundo no cita ningún hecho y el tercero describe algo comprobable.

pairs: I noticed that you lost the ball three times.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué fue útil el comentario de Leo.

choices.text: It was much longer and more polite than the manager's comment.
It praised her for speaking quickly and clearly.
It described what he noticed and gave her a step to take.

feedback.es: Leo cita un hecho (habló rápido en el medio) y propone pasos (respirar, añadir un ejemplo): específico y accionable.

origin.audio: At the volunteer meeting, Sara gave a short presentation. Afterwards, her manager said: That was confusing. Leo, who was sitting next to her, tried again: I noticed that you spoke quickly in the middle, so next time, take a breath before each new idea, and I suggest you add one example. Sara nodded.

prompt.es: Con la misma escena, elige qué se deduce del comentario del jefe «That was confusing».

choices.text: It is vague: it gives an impression but not what to change.
It is disrespectful because it attacks Sara as a person in public.
It is useful because it tells her to explain more.

feedback.es: «Confusing» expresa una impresión sin decir qué cambiar; no ataca a Sara ni propone un paso concreto.

origin.audio: At the volunteer meeting, Sara gave a short presentation. Afterwards, her manager said: That was confusing. Leo, who was sitting next to her, tried again: I noticed that you spoke quickly in the middle, so next time, take a breath before each new idea, and I suggest you add one example. Sara nodded.

prompt.es: Completa: «Un comentario es accionable cuando propone un paso que puedes dar mañana.»

feedback.es: Actionable describe lo que se puede poner en práctica de inmediato: un paso concreto, no un deseo general.

origin.text: Telling someone You need to improve does not help much. A comment is ___ only when it names a step that you can take tomorrow.

prompt.es: Lee el correo y elige qué criterio incumple principalmente.

choices.text: It is vague: it never says how late Tom was.
It is disrespectful: it judges Tom's attitude instead of describing facts.
It is too long and gives Tom several tasks at once.

feedback.es: El correo sí dice cuánto llegó tarde (veinte minutos); lo que falla es que juzga la actitud de Tom.

origin.text: Email to a volunteer: Hi Tom, you were twenty minutes late, again. You clearly do not care about this project. Please fix this.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la niña sobre el comentario «Try harder».

choices.text: That it was disrespectful and made her leave the old club at once.
That it was too specific for a player of her age.
That it was vague and did not tell her how to improve.

feedback.es: «Try harder» no dice qué cambiar; el nuevo comentario sí (frenar al final), y por eso le motiva.

origin.audio: A coach told a girl: Your start was fast, but you rushed the final part. Tomorrow, let's practise slowing down together. The girl smiled. At her old club, the coach only said: Try harder. She told her mother that this new feedback was the first that made her want to train.

prompt.es: Lee la situación y elige la versión mejorada del comentario «Good job».

choices.text: Good job: I noticed that you answered every question calmly; next time, add an example.
Good job, you are clearly the best speaker in the whole group, and everyone knows it.
Good job, but your answers were terrible in the middle.

feedback.es: La versión mejorada cita un hecho y propone un paso; las otras son elogio vago o ataque.

origin.text: A manager wants to improve the comment Good job, which she wrote after a colleague's interview. She wants it to be specific and actionable, but still respectful.

prompt.es: Completa: «Te sugiero que practiques tu pie izquierdo dos veces por semana.»

feedback.es: I suggest you + verbo base formula una recomendación concreta sin ser una orden.

origin.text: The coach does not give an order. She says, in a calm and respectful voice: I ___ you practise your left foot twice a week.
